title: Water Treatment Specialist (Water Trmt SPC)
raw_text:
10-92W. MOS 92W--Water Treatment Specialist (Water Trmt SPC), CMF 92 (Eff 202510)
    a. Major duties. The Water Treatment Specialist is primarily responsible for supervising and installing water
purification equipment, ensuring clean water storage and availability, and performing water quality tests to detect
potential contaminants. They also inspect facilities and food suppliers for disease-causing agents, germs, and
environmental hazards. In Field Hospitals, they serve as laundry equipment operators, overseeing the sanitary
operation of laundry facilities to maintain health and hygiene standards, safeguarding public health and preventing
the spread of waterborne diseases. Duties for MOS 92W at each level of skill are:
         (1) MOSC 92W1O. Collect and test water samples, following established procedures. Operate and
maintain basic water purification equipment, assisting with setup and breakdown. Monitor water quality indicators,
reporting deviations to supervisors. Maintain records of testing results and equipment maintenance. Follow safety
protocols while handling chemicals and operating equipment. Support overall facility operations and sanitation
efforts. Assist with basic laundry facility operations.
         (2) MOSC 92W2O. Purify water using various treatment methods, ensuring potable water standards.
Operate and perform preventative maintenance on a wider range of water treatment equipment. Analyze water
samples, interpret results and adjust treatment processes. Supervise small teams in water purification tasks,
providing guidance and training. Inspect facilities and food suppliers for basic sanitation concerns. Maintain
inventory of chemicals and supplies, managing stock levels. Operate laundry equipment facilities, ensuring
sanitary operation.
         (3) MOSC 92W3O. Supervise water purification operations, ensuring quality control and compliance with
regulations. Direct water reconnaissance efforts, identifying and developing new water sources. Troubleshoot and
repair complex water treatment equipment malfunctions. Train and mentor junior soldiers in water treatment
procedures. Analyze water quality data, prepare reports and recommendations. Manage operation and quality
control of water supply, storage, distribution, and purification activities at battalion/brigade level. Employ CBRN
detection and purification techniques to ensure water sources are free from chemical, biological, radiological, and
nuclear contamination.
         (4) MOSC 92W4O. Manage all aspects of water treatment facilities, including personnel, equipment, and
resources. Develop and implement water treatment plans, adapting to changing conditions. Advise commanders
on water supply issues, providing technical expertise. Direct water reconnaissance and water point development
for division, corps, and echelons above corps. Oversee quality control programs, maintaining compliance with
standards. Furnish reports to higher headquarters. Develop area water supply and treatment plans and supervise
operation. Perform staff and advisory duties related to water and laundry operations.
    b. Physical demands rating and qualifications for the initial award of MOS. Water treatment specialists must
possess the following qualifications:
         (1) A physical demands rating of Significant (Gray).
         (2) A physical profile of 211221.
         (3) Normal color vision.
         (4) Qualifying scores.
             (a) A minimum score of 88 in aptitude area GM.
             (b) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) – 0140 cm, Seated Power Throw (PT) – 0400
cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0140 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) – 0040 shuttles in Physical Demand
Category in “Significant” (Gray).
         (5) Mandatory formal training. Completion of MOS 92W course conducted under the auspices of the U.S.
Army Quartermaster School; or meet the ACASP criteria listed in AR 601-210. Waiver requests can be submitted
to the Office of the Quartermaster Commandant Enlisted Proponent Office at USARMY Ft Lee VA, 23801.
TRADOC List QM Enlisted Personnel Development lee.tradoc.list.qm-enlisted-personnel-development@army.mil.
    c. Additional skill identifiers.
         (1) D6--Operational Data Analyst (personnel only)
    d. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to each skill level are
listed in the following tables:
         (1) Table 10-92W-1. Physical requirements.
         (2) Table 10-92W-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
         (3) Table 10-92W-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
